units.P1: excluded: product summary; installing, updating and removing modules and their sources are owned by the load, install, update, uninstall and package-sources pages

ipm.reason: Root summary of IPM. Its child ipm.shell and the feature pages (load, install, update, uninstall, architecture/package-sources) own every behavior it names. No additional obligation.

obligations.text: Users run commands in the zpm shell or as zpm "<command>"; programs call %IPM.Main:Shell(), which returns a status showing whether the command succeeded.
Only %IPM.Main:Shell() lets a script see that a command failed: Shell(command) returns the status, and Shell(command, 1) also ends the process with exit code 1 on failure.
obligations.cases: Shell vs Shell(,1) vs command/function forms; failing vs passing command
obligations.observation: returned status, process exit code, continuation
obligations.basis: reused:.g5/ontology/features/package-commands.g5.md metadata (iter5 entry_forms.rs); iteration-72 rule-4a re-audit (G5): partial, support inspection
obligations.gap: Rule 4a (iteration-72): The exclusivity claim ("only Shell lets a script see a failure") rests on constant rows for the command and function forms. How the arguments reach Shell and the terminate flag are not computed.

obligations.text: The zpm "<command>" command form discards the status; adding ,1 does not pass a flag, so the process keeps running and exits 0.
obligations.cases: zpm "cmd" vs zpm "cmd",1 on a failing command
obligations.basis: reused:.g5/ontology/features/package-commands.g5.md metadata (iter5 entry_forms.rs); iteration-72 rule-4a re-audit (G5): partial, support inspection
obligations.gap: Rule 4a (iteration-72): That ,1 does not reach Shell is written down as a constant row. The %ZLANGC00 argument passing is not modelled.

obligations.text: As built (C:D24), the $zpm("<command>") function form runs the command, then fails with <COMMAND> Function must return a value whether the command passed or failed.
obligations.cases: pinned lowercase body vs capitalized body; passing vs failing command
